text.en:
Meena felt hot and tired. Her mother touched her forehead and said, "I think you have a fever, but touch can be wrong."
She placed a thermometer under Meena's tongue for a minute. It showed 38.5 degrees Celsius.
"Now we know for sure," said her mother.

Temperature tells us how hot or cold something is. Our sense of touch can be wrong, so we use a thermometer.
Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius (written °C). Water freezes at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C.
A laboratory thermometer has a bulb with a liquid inside a thin tube. When the bulb gets hot, the liquid rises in the tube. We read the scale at the top of the liquid.
A clinical thermometer is used for body temperature. Normal human body temperature is about 37 °C. A clinical thermometer is not used for hot water because it reads only about 35 °C to 42 °C.
Before using a clinical thermometer, shake it so that the liquid goes below 35 °C. After use, wash it and keep it safely. Hold a laboratory thermometer upright and do not let the bulb touch the glass.
Temperature tells how hot or cold something is. Touch can mislead us, so we use a thermometer.

board.text: hot or cold? use a thermometer

text.en: We measure temperature in degrees Celsius. Water freezes at zero and boils at one hundred.
A clinical thermometer is for the body. Normal body temperature is about thirty-seven degrees.
Shake the clinical thermometer before use, and read the scale where the liquid ends.

problem.en: A thermometer shows 39 °C for a child. Is the child's temperature normal?

why.en: A higher value means the body is hotter than normal.

text.en: So it is not normal; the child may have a fever and should see a doctor.

why.en: A temperature this high needs care.

prompt.en: A friend wants to measure boiling water with a clinical thermometer. What will you tell him?

requiredIdeas.en: A clinical thermometer reads only about 35 to 42 degrees Celsius.
Boiling water is about 100 °C, so the thermometer could break; use a laboratory thermometer.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking all thermometers work for all temperatures.

points.en: Water freezes at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C.
Shake a clinical thermometer before using it.
